item.title: Myantharun's Mandala-Manifested Meadow of Majestic, Melancholic Madness: Re: Myantharun's Mandala-Manifested Meadow of Majestic, Melancholic Madness
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

The discovery section doesn't actually mention the SCP at all. Like, there's not even anything which like is referenced as a mandala or anything so it just kinda feels weird?

This means the addendum in the first iteration doesn't flow right because we haven't seen a SCP-XXXX mandala yet so there's not a clear thing that the dream team can like…do to go to SCP-XXXX-1?

The second iteration feels really unsatisfying as a whole: it feels like it doesn't quite build off the first one in a way that grants closure so much as is just kinda…confusing? Like, idk, I guess my question is why a SCP file for this anomaly exists but Dream Team aren't made aware of what Ara Orun are up to; or well, really, why the conflict between the two continues like why don't they just talk to each other? It's not like one of these files is more classified than the other, at least according to the ACS.

I like the first iteration generally; it feels lacking as a whole but it has some really nice 'descent into dreamland' vibes and I enjoy it; but iteration 2 doesn't really build off it so much as feel like it's the narrative equivalent of hitting a brick wall while you're going at 90 on the highway?

This said: it also feels a lot like this is a kinda generic dream entity and I'm not sure if that's just because I don't really get what's happening here on a metaphorical level?

Coherence

Mostly fine; it feels like it's all kinda centred around a single thing and escalation situation and stuff; a few things I've mentioned above are a little iffy from this perspective too but they're relatively easily to fix.

Consistency

Not quite sure what you mean by this; but the internal logic of the piece feels like it's being kept consistent and the rules aren't suddenly changing or anything.

Dialogue

It's fine? There's not really any lines that stand out as being hugely memorable or anything; but there's equally no lines which feel hugely clunky or anything.

The characters could perhaps do with more of a personality: they're like, obviously different because of what they can do but they aren't all that different in terms of how they talk or what they're like as people.

Clinical tone

Yeah basically fine. See the LBL for some minor things.

Pacing & Plot & Second list page

See earlier comments.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

SCP-XXXX and its related anomalies are undetectable by most individuals without sufficient anti-memetics training, therefore standard visual containment is not required.

'related anomalies' feels vague here in an unsatisfying way: do you mean -1 and -2? do you mean a whole bunch of other antimemetic SCPs?

Also, I'm not necessarily sure that the lack of visual containment does necessarily follow here? Like I'm sure it does when a reader sees the actual properties and stuff; but in this isolated bit, it stands out as weird because like…we can still be affected by stuff we can't detect (e.g., if you drain all the air out a room, we might not be able to see that but we can certainly be affected by it).

This particularly feels janky when the next sentence implies it can be seen sometimes! So why don't they lock it up just in case?

In rare circumstances, such as under the influence of psychedelics, visibility of SCP-XXXX is possible.

"In rare circumstances,…, SCP-XXXX can be visually detected.' would probably flow better: 'visibility' feels like a gradient rather than a binary, and possible feels iffy when talking gradients.

are to be amnesticized and monitored for any significant and abrupt changes

'significant or abrupt' might be better here but but *shrugs*

as well as for signs of psychosis

SCP-XXXX Is an anomalous mandala

rogue capital

a graphic and often symbolic pattern usually in the form of a circle divided into four separate sections or bearing a multiple projection of an image.

'bearing a multiple projection of an image' is janky but I'm not exactly sure how best to fix it

I would also generally lean towards capitalising the first word of a footnote.

that has been observed appearing in multiple population centers.

I feel like this is a touch vague about what it actually is? Like is it just…an image that appears a lot in posters? Is it a weird 2d image entity that moves around?

Every instance of SCP-XXXX is identical in pattern, coloration and size.

this feels a little unsatisfying because it's never actually like, described in any way: like I get putting an image of it in the file is probably a bad idea but like…there's not even a vague description of what it includes.

SCP-XXXX-2 is an entity of varying form that is located in SCP-XXXX-1. Its form is that a young humanoid woman with wings on its back that resemble those of a blue butterfly. (Blue Morpho)

Does it have varying form or is it's form that of a young woman with wings on its back that resemble those of a blue butterfly?

IMO: you can cut humanoid here; if you say 'young woman', people will assume 'human' or at least 'human adjacent'.

I'd also have the 'blue morpho' before the full stop; or potentially as the main text with a footnote explaining it's a butterfly

MTF Omicron Rho ("The Dream Team") discovered SCP-XXXX-2 in their deployment into SCP-XXXX-1. See addenda.

I'd probably cut this since the conflation between this and the discovery right after feels…confusing? Like in the sense that this introduces a second discovery event right before you introduce the first.

When the congregation underwent substantial changes in behavior while the parishioners were in prayer.

This is a sentence fragment that's missing what happened when said substantial changes occurred.

Another significant portion of the congregation attempted

I feel like specifying an approximate number instead of 'significant' would be more effective here.

to eat portions of the marble pews3 Traces of blood and fragments of broken teeth were discovered at the site of this incident.

this footnote is unnecessary and you're missing a period.

I also feel like the flow of information is weird: I think noting that it's hypothesised that people tried to eat the pews based of the blood/teeth fragments at the site would work better; or like, indicating that the eating caused there to be said traces left or something.

After this incident, the Foundation dispatched field agents to survey the surroundings

This phrasing kinda implies that the Foundation knew about the incident in some magical manner and immediately dispatched agents after it occurred; it feels like this needs an intermediate step like e.g. embedded agents in the police department diverting this to the foundation or something.

I'd also be tempted to put a number of agents in here; or refer to a single field agent say.

Their comms devices were discovered drenched in an unseen fluid that could only be detected by Foundation psychics.

This feels weird to me; like, the further in we get, the less saying they were discovered 'drenched' feels like it makes sense. Also 'unseen' is unnecessary if only psychics can detect it; it implies it could be e.g. felt whereas the later part indicates it can't even be felt.

Exploration Video Log Transcript

I'd probably trim the 'exploration team' and 'subject' fields and instead add a short summary of the purpose of this: like, why are Omicron Rho being sent in? Is their job 'to identify anomalies within SCP-XXXX-1' or 'to explore -1' or 'to recover someone from -1' or?

Dream Team moves toward locked wooden door.

IMO: not having a 'The' at the start here feels a little wonky.

House, Hero and Operator lean against the wall next to the door.

Listing the names like this implies there's more team members than just those three here

They slowly open the door and peer through the crack.

This was described as a 'locked wooden door' a second earlier; how are they opening it now?

The nun walks over to the door and opens it.

What door is this? The only one mentioned has already been opened?

Operator: <Operator takes several pictures of the fluid and saves them to her folder.>

FOOTAGE LOST

I'd probably centre this

<Operator slowly approaches a sedated young woman.

Missing the > at the end here

save for a Mandala symbol that appears tattooed onto its face

Is this a SCP-XXXX mandala or a different mandala?

//<Hero turns around, telekinetically lifts chunks of dirt and rocks out of the ground and throwing them into the distance.

Missing the closing > and //

This action, and the following stuff, feels…completely disconnected from what was happening just before it in a slightly unsatisfying way

Dream Team appears in what resembles medieval Europe

'appears somewhere that resembles' might parse better here

House: <Erects a brick wall from the ground, stopping a citizen who was mid-flight.>

IMO: cut the dialogue tag and just use the action but with 'House' at the start.

Then again, this just…feels odd for House to do?

Operator pulls House by the collar of his fatigues and pulls him backwards.

I'd change the first 'pulls' to 'grabs', or cut the 'and pulls him' and move 'backwards' to just after 'House'.

House's leg gets caught in the serpent's form,

How does it get caught? This feels weirdly passive

Operator: <Operator continues dragging House.>

Probably the last time I'll mention this but the dialogue tag can be cut here and anywhere you do this.

launching every citizen around him.

this feels like it's missing something like 'into the air' at the end; like, words indicating where the citizens go, y'know?

Hero frees himself from the large man's hold

this feels weirdly lacking in description of how it's done

standing underneath an instance of SCP-XXXX.

this is altogether far too far into this SCP for this to be the first explicitly mentioned instance of SCP-XXXX (there's been a few mandalas that could be the scp but nothing concrete)

<SCP-XXXX-2 steps back and stares at the stone circle.>//

missing opening //

FOOTAGE LOST

the last one in the document is missing the lines before/after it.

Iteration 1

Mobile Task Force Omega-0 ("Ará Orún") is to be deployed into SCP-XXXX-1 by using SCP-XXXX as entryways.

deployed into -1 to do what?

SCP-XXXX-3 is to be forcibly contained within SCP-XXXX-1 and redirected back into SCP-XXXX-2.

Something about the flow of this feels janky; but I think it's just that we haven't had the new -1 and -2 established so -2 being a thing that exists in -1 isn't like,,, something we're sure of yet?

All efforts are to be focused on a permanent solution to SCP-XXXX-2's rapidly deteroriating condition.

I feel like something more specific than 'rapidly deteriorating condition' would be good here: really show what's happening in an evocative way, y'know?

Its primary locations for spawning include but are not limited to

something about this feels iffy; maybe "It primarily appears in the following locations:" would be better?

  • Mass congregations.
  • Cults.

These feel…vague for locations?

SCP-XXXX is the pathway between SCP-XXXX-1 and reality.

My general feeling is that you have to say what -1 is before you can say this; perhaps saing e.g. "pathway between the collective unconsciousness (designated SCP-XXXX-1) and reality" would be best?

Addendum:

I would add line breaks between the paragraphs here just to space it out a little.

[-] Line By Line

Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: SCP draft Crit: Re: SCP draft Crit
item.content:encoded:
Hello there,

due to clinical tone not being my forte I shall refrain from judging it. But I do like the concept and the visual it paints. The flow of the sentences is continuous and matches the current atmosphere you are aiming for. Although this kind of writing style might not be my preference. Still, this aspect is more of a subjective evaluation.

Storywise I think it makes for an interesting SCP and I like the idea of the changing classes. But to me, it feels like it is one image too much. I personally think that its effect could be stronger if the jump between them felt cruder and less caring.

All in all, I do enjoy the "Ferryman" you have painted here. The story itself has just enough ambiguousness left and captures a certain hunger for me, at least in me.

Good luck with your story.

item.title: Lot of Sodom: Re: Lot of Sodom
item.content:encoded:
Okay, so this seems good so far. I figure I should leave my thoughts, while I'm here.

+ Sure, Why Not?
- Oops, misclick

I feel the personnel are being unusually sympathetic to this creature, at least in both breach logs. I remember the foundations is meant to be "cold, not cruel", so maybe have them be more blunt and display less affection. My perception of security would be more rough and forceful, unless containment procedures explicitly states requirements of expressions of empathy to re-contain subject.
Though the last two logs I felt nailed this mark fairly well, and left enough clues to be interesting. Maybe some more information would be appreciated of the creature's circumstances and how it displays its anomalous properties in greater detail, especially for people that may be less initiated with the Lots of Sodom.

item.title: Draft: Frozen Corpse and Nervous System: Draft: Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
Greenlight thread:
http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13886219/greenlight-request-frozen-corpse-and-nervous-system

Sandbox article:
http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/gopher-chucks

Sorry for the wait on this; the holiday season was busy, the audio took some time to record/edit, and I took a while to figure out the Sandbox.

Anyway, this is my first completed draft of my SCP hopeful. I'm hoping for an overall review, but a few specific things I'm hoping to hear about:
-I intended to make the skip both unnerving and sympathetic to the reader/listener. How did I do?
-I presented the series of events in relatively vague terms, and in the order of the Foundation learning about them, which is out of chronological order, so that the reader can piece together the story on their own. Am I being too obvious, not obvious enough, or is there another issue in how this is presented?
-Is the length okay? (word count is 2496)

Also, just a general question, since I couldn't find a clear answer in the guides, but does a draft need an official greenlight before being uploaded to the site, or can it be uploaded as soon as the writer is confident in it?

Thanks!

item.title: SCP draft Crit: Re: SCP draft Crit
item.content:encoded:
Hi there!

Before I start I'd just like to mention that I'm not a verified reviewer or greenlighter, but I do have some feedback.

Overall, I'd give this article a solid 8.5/10. I really enjoy the overall story of it. The changing of the items class and danger as the article goes on is really intriguing. I also enjoy the repeating theme of the Ferryman (I'm guessing thats an allusion to SCP-XXXX-1?)

The sentences also flow quite smoothly. The only issue that I'd point out is the sentence "Due to the difficulty of boarding SCP-XXXX-2, there have been recorded at least four individuals to successfully board the vehicle in every SCP-XXXX event." I feel as if the wording in the first half of the sentence could be changed a tiny bit to display that barely anyone is able to board SCP-XXXX-2. Possibly, "…only approximately four individuals are able to sucessfully board SCP-XXXX-2 in every SCP-XXXX event" or something similar to that.

Otherwise, I really did enjoy reading this article, and hope to see it succeed in future.

Good luck,
Mofi

item.title: The Black Hourglass: Re: The Black Hourglass
item.content:encoded: Thanks for the suggestions and critique. Although, I'm a bit curious as to what you meant by "(now I know why you named him 'Licht'." I'll admit I didn't choose the name entirely at random, and I'm aware of its origin and direct meaning, as well as a few characters from different pieces of media with the same name. But since the ones I know of don't have much to do with my article or this character arc, I was just wondering if there was some other character or person that I unintentionally made a parallel to.
